correctness.rationale: The row Gram matrix has diagonal |B| and off-diagonal entry P_B(zeta^d). For d with valuation v, zeta^d is primitive of order p^(k-v), so its rational minimal polynomial Phi_{p^(k-v)} divides the integer mask precisely when that off-diagonal vanishes. Distinct required cyclotomic factors are pairwise coprime; their product divides P_B, and evaluating at one shows p^{|R(A)|} divides |B|. Conversely the proposed digit set has mask product over the required Phi_{p^s}; uniqueness of base-p digit expansions makes all coefficients 0 or 1 and keeps the exponents inside Z/(p^k). It therefore gives the matching tight frame. The singleton case has an empty scale set and minimum one. The frozen verifier exhausts Z/4, Z/8 and Z/9 and checks larger constructions, but the proof is general.

evidence: Each required distinct cyclotomic factor is monic and coprime to the others, so their product divides the mask; evaluation at one contributes one factor p per required scale.
The free-digit set has mask exactly the product of those cyclotomic factors and gives a 0-1 subset because the chosen base-p digit positions are independent.

evidence: Tightness is equivalent to vanishing of the off-diagonal row Gram sums at every nonzero difference of A.
For a difference with p-adic valuation v, the relevant root has exact order p^(k-v), so the vanishing condition is exactly divisibility of the 0-1 mask by Phi_{p^(k-v)}.

value.rationale: Minimum oversampling for a tight exponential frame is a natural finite-harmonic invariant. The theorem gives a complete closed form for every subset of every cyclic prime-power group and an explicit optimizer controlled only by the intrinsic p-adic difference scales, which is reusable structure rather than a finite calculation.

final_claim: For every nonempty A in Z/(p^k), the minimum cardinality of a distinct-frequency tight exponential frame for C^A is p^{|R(A)|}, where R(A) is the set of p-adic valuations of nonzero differences; tightness is equivalent to the corresponding cyclotomic divisibilities, and the stated free-base-p-digit set attains the minimum.
